summary: The manna aggadah concludes: Joshua received manna for all Israel; daily provision kept Israel dependent on God. The Gemara transitions to Yom Kippur afflictions, establishing that the five afflictions correspond to five verses of inuy, and that drinking is subsumed under eating.

display.title: Daily Manna Builds Daily Relationship

learning.ahaMoment: Scarcity is a relationship tool: God used daily manna to build daily intimacy with Israel.
learning.memoryAnchor: Son visits daily for bread, once a year for a gift - manna kept Israel returning.
learning.learnerQuestion: Why did God give manna daily instead of a year's supply at once?
learning.coreTension: Between practical convenience (a year's supply means no daily labor) and the spiritual goal of continuous dependence and daily prayer.
learning.coreMove: Rabbi Shimon's parable makes the logic explicit: a father who gives his son everything at once is visited once a year; a father who gives daily is visited daily. Daily manna was a relationship technology - it required Israel to return to God every morning.

takeaway.text: Daily dependence creates daily relationship. The manna was calibrated not for convenience but to make prayer a genuine necessity rather than a habit.

learning.learningBlocker: Students may focus on the inconvenience and miss that the limitation was deliberate and purposeful.

quizSeeds.question: Why did manna fall daily rather than once a year?
quizSeeds.answer: So that Israel would pray to God daily for their needs; annual provision would produce only annual prayer

sugyot.finalRuling: Non-halachic aggadah: daily manna was designed to create daily prayer and constant divine dependence.

display.title: Tarfon Challenges Elazar on Manna Volume

learning.ahaMoment: Every analogy carries the burden of proving it is apt; Tarfon's challenge is a lesson in analogy-vetting.
learning.memoryAnchor: Tarfon challenges the Flood comparison: show the parallel is sound before the number stands.
learning.learnerQuestion: How did the rabbis calculate the total volume of manna, and why does the method matter?
learning.coreTension: Between Rabbi Elazar's derivation of manna volume by analogy from the Flood and Rabbi Tarfon's challenge that the analogy is internally inconsistent.
learning.coreMove: The debate is about the standard for a valid derivation by analogy. Tarfon argues that the Flood comparison succeeds only if the two situations share the same operative feature; an inconsistency in the parallel defeats the derivation.

takeaway.text: A quantitative derivation by analogy requires that the parallel case share the same operative feature; a demonstrated inconsistency in the analogy defeats the derivation.

learning.learningBlocker: Students may focus on the quantity (how much manna fell) and miss the methodological argument about how analogies work.

argumentFlow.speaker: Gemara
argumentFlow.text: Flood: forty days; manna: one hour - different scales

quizSeeds.question: Why does Isi ben Yehuda consider the manna a greater miracle than the Flood?
quizSeeds.answer: The Flood took forty days to occur; the manna's equivalent provision fell in a single hour - far more concentrated and miraculous

sugyot.finalRuling: Non-halachic aggadah: manna's hourly miracle surpasses the Flood's forty-day event.

display.whats: Isi ben Yehuda: manna in one hour; five YK afflictions and drinking subsumed under eating
display.hint: Why does the mishna list only five afflictions when six are forbidden? Is drinking included in eating?
display.title: Manna Greater Than the Flood

learning.ahaMoment: Halakhic derivation can follow physiological logic: eating and drinking share the same oral mechanism, so one prohibition covers both.
learning.memoryAnchor: Eating includes drinking - one verse, one body, two Yom Kippur prohibitions.
learning.learnerQuestion: How can a single verse about eating on Yom Kippur prohibit both eating and drinking?
learning.coreTension: Between the need for each prohibition to have its own explicit source and the possibility of deriving two prohibitions from a single verse.
learning.coreMove: The Gemara reasons that eating normally includes drinking (physiologically intertwined acts); a prohibition on eating therefore extends to drinking when both fall under the same bodily category of oral intake.

takeaway.text: When two acts are physiologically intertwined, a prohibition stated for one can extend to the other by analogy of function - one verse, one body mechanism, two prohibitions.

learning.learningBlocker: Students may expect a separate explicit verse for drinking and be surprised that the eating verse can cover it.

argumentFlow.text: Food and drink listed together under one category

argumentFlow.label: Sheikhar verse implies drinking is separate
argumentFlow.speaker: Gemara
argumentFlow.text: 'Sheikhar' in the verse separates drink from food

halachic: five YK afflictions correspond to five inuy verses
drinking subsumed under eating as a category

quizSeeds.question: If the mishna lists six forbidden activities on Yom Kippur, why are there only five afflictions?
quizSeeds.answer: Drinking is subsumed under eating - both are forms of taking physical pleasure through consumption, counted as one category

sugyot.finalRuling: Drinking is subsumed under eating; five afflictions correspond to five Torah verses of inuy.

glossary.en: Affliction or self-denial; the Torah uses this term in multiple contexts (Yom Kippur, metzora, Egypt) which the Gemara interprets through verbal analogy.
Strong drink or intoxicating beverage; used in a verse to distinguish drinking from eating.
Section or passage of the Torah; the Gemara cites five separate passages using the word inuy.

rashiTranslations.he: זה יהושע. שעלה עם משה עד תחומי ההר שנאמר (שמות כד)
rashiTranslations.en: 'This is Joshua' - who ascended with Moses up to the mountain's boundary, as it is stated (Exodus 24),

rashiTranslations.he: ויקם משה ויהושע משרתו ויעל משה אל הר סיני והמתין לו
rashiTranslations.en: 'And Moses arose, and Joshua his attendant, and Moses went up to Mount Sinai'; and Joshua waited for him

rashiTranslations.he: יהושע שם כל מ' יום שנאמר וישמע יהושע את קול העם ברעה
rashiTranslations.en: there for all forty days, as it is stated, 'and Joshua heard the voice of the people as they shouted,'

rashiTranslations.he: למדנו שלא היה עמהם ושם היה יורד לו מן כנגד כל ישראל: עד
rashiTranslations.en: from which we learn he was not with them, and there manna fell for him equal to all of Israel. 'How

rashiTranslations.he: מתי אתה מגבב דברים ומביא עלינו.
rashiTranslations.en: long will you heap up words and bring upon us'

rashiTranslations.he: מאין לך: חמש עשרה אמה מלמעלה.
rashiTranslations.en: - from where do you derive it? 'Fifteen cubits above'

rashiTranslations.he: אם תאמר מלמעלה לארץ ולא פירש
rashiTranslations.en: - if you say 'above' means above the earth, but it did not specify

rashiTranslations.he: בהר או בבקעה וכי חמש עשרה בהר.
rashiTranslations.en: whether on a mountain or in a valley, was it fifteen cubits on the mountain

rashiTranslations.he: וכו': תיבה היכי סגיא. היאך עלתה
rashiTranslations.en: etc.? 'How did the ark travel' - how did it rise

rashiTranslations.he: לראשי ההרים אלא על כרחך מלמעל'
rashiTranslations.en: to the mountaintops? Rather, you must say 'above'

rashiTranslations.he: דקרא מן השמים הוא והכי קאמר
rashiTranslations.en: in the verse means above from the heavens, and this is what it means:

rashiTranslations.he: על ידי גשמים גברו ט"ו אמה ומן
rashiTranslations.en: through rain, the waters rose fifteen cubits, and from

rashiTranslations.he: התהום יצאו תחלה למלאות הבקעות
rashiTranslations.en: the deep they first emerged to fill the valleys

rashiTranslations.he: והשפלות עד שהשוו לראשי ההרים:
rashiTranslations.en: and lowlands until they reached the level of the mountaintops.

rashiTranslations.he: מרובה. רבה על חברתה מדה טובה
rashiTranslations.en: 'Greater' - greater than its counterpart; a good measure

rashiTranslations.he: מרובה על הרעה חמש מאות בה
rashiTranslations.en: is five hundred times greater than a punishing one,

rashiTranslations.he: שבמדה טובה נאמר (שם לד) נוצר
rashiTranslations.en: since regarding a good measure it is stated (there, 34), 'He preserves

rashiTranslations.he: חסד לאלפים ובמדת פורענות הוא
rashiTranslations.en: kindness for thousands,' while regarding a punishing measure it

rashiTranslations.he: אומר על שלשים ועל רבעים אף
rashiTranslations.en: says 'upon the third and fourth generations'; so too

rashiTranslations.he: כאן מדת הטוב של ירידת המן
rashiTranslations.en: here, the measure of goodness of the manna's descent

rashiTranslations.he: רבתה על ירידת המבול: במדת
rashiTranslations.en: was greater than the Flood's descent. 'Regarding the measure

rashiTranslations.he: פורענות הוא אומר וארובות השמים.
rashiTranslations.en: of punishment it says, and the windows of heaven'

rashiTranslations.he: לא ירד מבול אלא דרך שתי ארובות:
rashiTranslations.en: - the Flood descended only through two windows.

rashiTranslations.he: ובמדה טובה הוא אומר דלתי שמים
rashiTranslations.en: 'And regarding the good measure it says, the doors of heaven

rashiTranslations.he: פתח. ותנא כמה ארובות יש באורך
rashiTranslations.en: he opened' - and it was taught: how many windows are there in the length

rashiTranslations.he: דלת ארבע הרי לב' דלתות ח'
rashiTranslations.en: of a door - four; so for two doors, eight

rashiTranslations.he: ארובות ואחרי ששתי ארובות הורידו
rashiTranslations.en: windows; and since two windows brought down

rashiTranslations.he: גשמים גובה ט"ו אמה ח' ארובות
rashiTranslations.en: rain to a height of fifteen cubits, eight windows

rashiTranslations.he: הורידו מן ששים אמות שהרי אמרת
rashiTranslations.en: brought down manna to sixty cubits, since you said

rashiTranslations.he: מדה טובה מרובה על של פורענות
rashiTranslations.en: the good measure is greater than the punishing one,

rashiTranslations.he: וכ"ש שאינה ממועטת הימנה: הא
rashiTranslations.en: and all the more so it is not less than it. 'This

rashiTranslations.he: לא דמיא. אדר' אלעזר המודעי
rashiTranslations.en: cannot be compared' - refers back to Rabbi Elazar HaModa'i's

rashiTranslations.he: קאי: פתיחה פתיחה גמר. מה
rashiTranslations.en: statement. 'He derived opening from opening' - just as

rashiTranslations.he: פתיחה האמורה בארובות המבול
rashiTranslations.en: the 'opening' stated regarding the Flood's windows

rashiTranslations.he: ט"ו לב' ארובות אף פתיחה האמורה
rashiTranslations.en: gave fifteen cubits for two windows, so too the 'opening' stated

rashiTranslations.he: בדלתות המן ט"ו אמה לכל ב'
rashiTranslations.en: regarding the manna's doors gave fifteen cubits for every two

rashiTranslations.he: ארובות: ובעשור. דחומש הפקודים
rashiTranslations.en: windows. 'And on the tenth' - from the Book of Numbers,

rashiTranslations.he: ואך בעשור דשור או כשב שבת
rashiTranslations.en: and 'but on the tenth' from the ox-or-sheep passage, 'a sabbath

rashiTranslations.he: שבתון וגו' בכולהו כתיב תענו
rashiTranslations.en: of complete rest,' etc. - in all of them it is written 'you shall afflict'

rashiTranslations.he: ועניתם: אניגרון. מין מאכל שנותנין
rashiTranslations.en: or 'and you shall afflict.' 'Anigron' - a kind of dish into which

rashiTranslations.he: בו יין ובכמה מקומות שנינו בתוספ'
rashiTranslations.en: wine is placed, and in several places we learned in the Tosefta

rashiTranslations.he: אניגרון ואכסיגרון שנותנין בו יין
rashiTranslations.en: 'anigron' and 'aksigron,' into which wine

rashiTranslations.he: ושמן: מיא דסילקא. מים ששלקו
rashiTranslations.en: and oil are placed. 'Beet water' - water in which

rashiTranslations.he: בהן תרדין: דכולהו שלקי. של שאר
rashiTranslations.en: chard was boiled. 'Of all boiled vegetables' - of other

rashiTranslations.he: מיני ירקי: מידי דמשכר. ואין שכרות
rashiTranslations.en: types of vegetables. 'Something intoxicating' - and drunkenness is not

rashiTranslations.he: דרך אכילה: קעילית. שם מקום:
rashiTranslations.en: the normal way of eating. 'Ke'ilit' - the name of a place.

rashiTranslations.he: חייב
rashiTranslations.en: 'Liable' - the daf ends mid-word here; the comment (explaining the liability via the priestly wine prohibition) continues on 76b.
